topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, sets out the scope of the lecture on the causes of cancer, and presents the core learning outcomes.

topics.label: The Interplay of Genetics, Environment, and Chance in Cancer Causation
topics.groupedBecause: Cancer development is driven by a combination of endogenous mutational processes, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures, as supported by population and migrant epidemiological data.

topics.label: Oncogenic Pathogens and the Etiology of Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: Infectious agents contribute to carcinogenesis through chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and disruptions of host cell proliferation, as exemplified by Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Mechanisms of DNA Damage and Metabolic Activation
topics.groupedBecause: Physical radiation and chemical carcinogens damage DNA directly or require endogenous xenobiotic metabolism to generate reactive intermediates that form bulky DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation versus Promotion and Non-Mutagenic Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: Non-mutagenic carcinogenic agents act as tumor promoters by inducing chronic inflammation or stimulating cellular proliferation pathways.

topics.label: Host Context, Developmental Stage, and Tissue-Specific Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: Carcinogenic outcomes depend on host biological context, including tissue-specific enzyme distribution, proliferative states during puberty, and reproductive history.

topics.label: Experimental and Epidemiological Methods for Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: Evaluating carcinogens and identifying exposures relies on genomic mutational signatures, population biobanks, in vivo animal models, and in vitro mutagenicity assays.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion: Environmental Risks and Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarising key takeaways regarding environmental risk, carcinogen potency, and everyday risk-benefit decision-making.
